title: Open Question on s((Z/kZ)^n) for fixed k
statement_text: It remains an interesting question to estimate $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)$ when $k$ is fixed and $n$ is large.
context_text: For a finite abelian group $G$ with exponent $\exp(G)$, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant $s(G)$ is the smallest integer $s$ such that every sequence of $s$ (not necessarily distinct) elements of $G$ has a subsequence of length $\exp(G)$ summing to zero; Erdős, Ginzburg and Ziv proved $s(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})=2k-1$. Geometrically, $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)$ is the least $s$ such that among any $s$ points of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$ one can choose $k$ whose centroid is a lattice point. Harborth proved $(k-1)2^n+1\le s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)\le(k-1)k^n+1$, with equality on the left for $k$ a power of 2; Reiher proved $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^2)=4k-3$; Alon and Dubiner proved $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)\le(cn\log n)^nk$ for an absolute constant $c$, so for fixed $n$ it grows linearly in $k$. Elsholtz obtained $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)\ge1.125^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}(k-1)2^n+1$ for odd $k\ge3$, in particular $\ge2.08^n$ for large $n$. Writing $r_3(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ for the largest size of a subset of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ with no three-term arithmetic progression, the authors prove $s((\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n)<3k(r_3(\mathbb{F}_{p_1}^n)+\dots+r_3(\mathbb{F}_{p_m}^n))$ where $p_1,\dots,p_m$ are the prime factors of $k$ (and $s(\mathbb{F}_p^n)\le2p\,r_3(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$); with the Ellenberg–Gijswijt bound $r_3(\mathbb{F}_p^n)\le(J(p)p)^n$, $0.8414\le J(p)\le0.9184$, this gives exponential upper bounds, but since $r_3(\mathbb{F}_p^n)\ge(p/2)^{(1-o(1))n}$ a large gap remains for odd $k\ge3$ and large $n$. This is additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.
notes: Stated as a general open problem in the field with no labeled environment; no specific attribution to prior work given.
paper_title: Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constants by avoiding three-term arithmetic progressions
